evals.name: eval-1-design-standard
evals.prompt: Pull orders from a CSV and a REST API into DuckDB, dedupe, and produce a daily revenue table.
evals.expected_output: Design mode, sized Standard. A spec in docs/design.md (plus ADRs in docs/adr/) built from the domain outward: derived numbers or open questions, a state diagram before the component flowchart, components labelled with the decisions they own, a boundary contract table, a context view (a flowchart, the system as a boundary subgraph) with the CSV and the API as two external-system nodes outside it, the default pattern taken from a template indexed in template-0-summaries (or an ADR saying why not). Every diagram parses. The reply ends with 'Approve or correct before I implement.' and no code is written.
assertions: The first line states design mode and the Standard size class
Every number that can change the design (row volumes, growth, refresh frequency, latency, memory) is derived with its arithmetic or listed as an open question; none is invented
The state diagram (stateDiagram-v2) of the domain entities comes before the component flowchart
Every component in the flowchart is labelled with the decision it owns
A boundary contract table (boundary | input | output | invariants | owner) has a row for every boundary in the flowchart

A context view drawn as a flowchart, with the system as a boundary subgraph, shows the CSV source and the REST API as two separate external-system nodes outside that subgraph; no Mermaid C4 diagram is used
The default pattern comes from a template found through template-0-summaries, or an ADR records why no template is followed
Every Mermaid diagram in the spec passes design-spec/skill/tools/validate_mermaid.mjs (exit 0)
The reply ends with "Approve or correct before I implement."
No code is written: the only files added are docs/design.md and ADRs under docs/adr/

evals.name: eval-2-small
evals.prompt: Script to convert one CSV to Parquet.
evals.expected_output: Sized Small: no spec, no ADR, no SQLMesh. One typed module and its tests written directly under the python-code-standards skill, passing the project's gates.
assertions: The first line states the Small size class
No docs/design.md, other spec, or ADR is written
No SQLMesh: no sqlmesh dependency, config, or models

The script is written directly, without a design step, and follows python-code-standards: ruff check, ruff format --check, the declarations checker, pyright, mypy and pytest with 100% statement and branch coverage of the new code all pass

evals.expected_output: Document mode on ParquetToXL at 8ffaa6f. assertions: Before docs/design.md is overwritten, the reply reports that the import direction changed: ports.py now imports from adapters

evals.name: eval-3b-document-planted-defects
evals.prompt: Document the design of this repository.
evals.expected_output: Document mode on the tally workspace. A dependency matrix over its five packages and the six findings in expected/eval-3b/answer-key.md, each with its rule number and file: tally-cli imports tally-core undeclared ('!'); tally-io declares tally-core unused ('d'); tally-stage declares tally-io unused ('d', known: BACKLOG.md item 2); tally-stage only forwards (rule 2); a dict crosses the core-to-io boundary (rule 4); the CLAUDE.md layering diagram disagrees with the code (rule 14). Deduced items marked inferred (in diagrams, a ` ?` label suffix and the dashed-border `inferred` classDef). No code changes.
assertions: All six defects in expected/eval-3b/answer-key.md are reported as findings, each with its rule number and file
Each finding is labelled new or known as the answer key says: only the unused tally-io declaration in tally-stage is known, citing BACKLOG.md item 2

Items deduced rather than read from the code (domain states, the decision each component owns) are marked inferred: *inferred* in text; in diagrams, a label ending in ` ?` plus the `inferred` classDef (stroke-dasharray, a dashed border), or one line above a diagram whose every node is inferred. No dashed arrow is used to mark inference
Every boundary in the contract table, every '!' or 'd' cell of the dependency matrix, and every component-flowchart node not marked inferred cites a path:line source
Every path:line the spec cites exists in the fixture at the build commit: the file is tracked there and has at least that many lines
No code is changed: git status shows changes to documentation files only

evals.name: eval-6-change-impact-planted-defects
evals.prompt: Restructure tally: remove the tally-stage pass-through and replace the dict that daily_revenue returns with a typed record. Design the change.
evals.expected_output: Design mode on an existing codebase: the tally workspace, built as for eval 3b, sized Standard (five packages). The spec in docs/design.md has a change-impact flowchart using classDef added, changed and removed: tally-stage removed; tally-core (returns the typed record), tally-io (writes it) and tally-cli (stops calling load_orders, drops tally-stage) changed; tally-common may be changed too if the record lives there; if the design adds a package or module (none is required), its added node names one that does not exist yet. Every diagram parses. The reply ends with 'Approve or correct before I implement.' and no code is written.
assertions: The first line states design mode and the Standard size class, and the spec treats tally as an existing codebase being restructured, not a new system
A change-impact flowchart defines classDef added, classDef changed and classDef removed
tally-stage is marked removed
tally-core, tally-io and tally-cli are each marked changed
Every changed or removed node names a workspace package (such as tally-stage) or module (such as tally_stage) that exists in the fixture, and every added node, if any, names one that does not
Every Mermaid diagram in the spec passes design-spec/skill/tools/validate_mermaid.mjs (exit 0)
The reply ends with "Approve or correct before I implement."
No code is written: git status and git diff <build commit> show changes to documentation files only
